parts.text: A student determines the mass M R of a metre ruler by a balancing method. He uses the apparatus shown in Fig. 1.1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The student places a circular load of mass M = 20 g on the metre ruler but in a position different from that shown in Fig. 1.1. Determine the distance d 0 of the centre of the load from the zero end of the ruler, as shown in Fig. 1.2. Fig. 1.2 is not to scale. d 0 = ................................................... cm [1]

ms.label: 1(b)(i)
ms.text: idea of allow to (just) tip one way then the other way / owtte

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The student determines the scale reading p on the ruler at the position of the pivot. He calculates the distance a between the 5.0 cm mark and the pivot and the distance b between the 50.0 cm mark and the pivot, using the equations a = p – 5.0 b = 50.0 – p . He repeats the procedure for values of M = 40 g, 60 g, 80 g and 100 g. His results are shown in Table 1.1. Table 1.1 M / g a / cm b / cm b a 20 39.5 5.5 40 35.7 9.3 0.26 60 32.6 12.4 0.38 80 29.0 16.0 0.55 100 27.0 18.0 0.67 For the value of M = 20 g, calculate and record in Table 1.1 the value of b a . [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Plot a graph of M / g ( y -axis) against b a ( x -axis). Draw the best-fit line. [4]
